items.title: FCC robot restrictions could accelerate shift to local AI
items.summary: A Unitree humanoid robot at the China Humanoid Robot Conference in Seoul in March. Robots are back in the national spotlight, and this time, the conversation is about more than what they can do. It’s about who controls them and what data they collect. The restrictions on foreign-produced robots by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) underscore the growing scrutiny of these machines as connected infrastructure. As robots take on more work in factories, warehouses, and other high-stakes environments, questions about how they use data and make decisions are becoming harder to ignore. That scrutiny is likely to accelerate the move toward on-premises AI architectures and smaller, specialized models that can run closer to where robots operate.
